content.title: Scan Passport Photo for Application on iPhone
content.meta_description: Learn how to crop and align passport and visa photos to official sizes like 2x2 in and 35x45 mm on iPhone and iPad with ID photo guides.
content.h1: How to Scan and Frame a Passport Photo for an Application
content.quick_answer: To prepare a passport photo on your iPhone, use ID photo mode to frame your face using the built-in guide. Select your target preset, such as 2x2 inches for the US or 35x45 mm for the UK and Schengen regions, then export a digital file or print sheet.
intro: Renewing a passport online requires a photo that strictly meets government framing standards. Submitting an uncropped snapshot or an incorrect aspect ratio can lead to immediate rejection by visa and passport processing portals.

This guide covers how to capture, frame, and crop a passport or visa headshot on iOS using preset dimensions. You will also learn how to choose between digital uploads and physical print sheets while keeping your personal images stored securely on your device.

If your goal is standard document capture rather than an identity headshot, you can scan standard paper documents without an app using built-in iOS tools. Otherwise, follow the steps below to prepare an identity photo.
content.steps_heading: How to Frame and Crop an ID Photo Using Document Scanner & PDF Toolkit

steps.title: Open ID photo mode
steps.detail: Select ID photo mode to activate the camera with the on-screen framing overlay. This overlay displays a face-position guide so you can align your head and chin correctly.

steps.title: Select your dimension preset
steps.detail: Choose the preset required by your issuing authority, such as 2x2 inches for United States documents or 35x45 mm for United Kingdom and Schengen visas. Make sure your preset matches your specific form instructions before shooting.

steps.title: Align your face with the guide
steps.detail: Position the iPhone so your eyes and head line up directly inside the face-position markers. Look straight into the camera lens with a neutral expression and ensure your entire head is visible.

steps.title: Capture or import the photo
steps.detail: Snap the picture using good ambient lighting, or import an existing clear portrait from your photo library. The app crops the image to the exact proportions of your chosen size preset.

steps.title: Export as a digital file or print sheet
steps.detail: Choose whether you need a single digital image file for an online application upload or a multi-photo print sheet for physical submission. Save the output directly to Files, Photos, or share it via AirDrop.

content.alternatives_heading: Alternative Methods for Getting a Passport Photo

alternatives.how: Upload a selfie to a web-based passport cropping website through a desktop or mobile browser.
alternatives.best_for: Quickly cropping an image when you are not using an iPhone or iPad.
alternatives.limitation: Online tools require uploading personal biometric identity photos to third-party servers, which introduces privacy concerns, and free versions often enforce daily usage limits.

alternatives.how: Take a photo against a plain wall and use the native crop tool in Apple Photos to estimate passport framing manually.
alternatives.best_for: Basic image cropping without installing any extra software.
alternatives.limitation: The built-in Photos app lacks biometric face-position guides and pre-configured international passport dimensions, making accurate alignment difficult.

content.features_heading: Key App Capabilities for Identity Photos

feature_points.benefit: Includes preset crops for 2x2 in and 35x45 mm standards alongside an on-screen face guide to keep your head size balanced.
Your facial portraits remain strictly on your iPhone, preventing private identity photos from being uploaded to external servers.
Allows you to export either a single digital image for online portals or a print sheet for paper applications, saving directly to local storage, iCloud Drive, or Files.

content.tips_heading: Tips for Preparing an Acceptable Passport Photo
tips: Stand facing a window or balanced light source to prevent harsh shadows behind your ears or under your chin.
Always double-check official government rules regarding eyeglasses, facial expressions, and head coverings, as regulations vary widely.
Verify whether your online portal expects a specific pixel range or file size, as digital upload requirements differ from physical photo cuts.

faqs.question: What are the standard passport photo sizes for the US, UK, and Schengen countries?
faqs.answer: The standard size for a United States passport photo is 2x2 inches (51x51 mm). For the United Kingdom, India, and Schengen countries, the standard dimension is 35x45 mm. Always check the issuing authority's official site for specific rules on recency and head size.

faqs.question: How does ID Photo mode align my head and face position?
faqs.answer: ID Photo mode overlays an on-screen face-position guide across the camera view. This allows you to position your chin, eyes, and crown within official proportions before capturing or cropping.

faqs.question: Can I export both a single digital photo file and a multi-photo print sheet?
faqs.answer: Yes. ID photo mode lets you export a single digital image file for web applications or generate a printable sheet containing multiple aligned copies for physical paper submissions.

faqs.question: Why is on-device photo processing important for official identity pictures?
faqs.answer: Passport photos contain sensitive biometric details. On-device processing keeps your pictures entirely on your local iOS storage instead of transmitting them to third-party web servers.

faqs.question: Where should I check for official background, glasses, and expression rules?
faqs.answer: Always confirm photo guidelines directly on the official website of your issuing government authority. Requirements regarding plain background colors, eyewear, and acceptable facial expressions differ by country and are updated regularly.
